name: Memory leak
description: A service keeps memory it no longer needs, so its memory use climbs until it hits the limit.
symptoms: Memory rising steadily on one service (positive slope of share-of-limit); latency creeps up late (GC pressure); traffic normal
distinguishing_clues: Steady slope that does not follow traffic (rps_ratio ~1) -> leak; memory that rises with traffic and falls after -> load, not leak
consequences_if_not_fixed: Out-of-memory kill -> service down -> failed requests and errors in every caller; repeats after each restart
typical_causes: Unbounded caches or lists, objects held by listeners, unclosed resources, native memory in libraries
time_to_impact: Minutes to days (predictable from the slope)
all_fixes: Restart with a helper copy (low risk, auto) | Scale out (low risk, auto) | Raise the resource limit (medium risk, ask) | Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench (part C), against no action only
eternalai_action: Predict time-to-limit; restart with a helper copy before the limit (automatic, low risk)
permanent_fix_by_human: Developer finds the leak with a heap profile and fixes the code; set memory limits and alerts
escalate_when: It returns within hours after restart, or started right after a deploy (then propose rollback)
how_to_reproduce: Chaos Mesh StressChaos memory / our leak endpoint
sources: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-memory-resource/ ; https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset)

name: CPU runaway / CPU hog
description: A process uses far more CPU than normal (busy loop, heavy regex, noisy neighbour), so requests queue up.
symptoms: CPU share near limit on one service, latency of that service up, throughput down; callers slower
distinguishing_clues: CPU up with flat traffic -> runaway; CPU up with traffic up -> overload. CPU high but node shared -> check neighbours (contention)
consequences_if_not_fixed: CPU throttling, timeouts in callers, possible cascading slowness
typical_causes: Infinite loop, catastrophic regex, hot retry loop, crypto/compression spike, noisy neighbour on the node
all_fixes: Restart with a helper copy (low risk, auto) | Scale out (low risk, auto) | Move the pod to another node (medium risk, ask) | Raise the resource limit (medium risk, ask) | Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask) | No action (watch only) (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench, but a close call: no action had 0% failed requests vs 0.7% with restart; restart only if users are affected
eternalai_action: Restart with a helper copy if user impact is visible; else watch (restart cost 0.7% failed requests in our bench vs 0% with no action)
permanent_fix_by_human: Profile and fix the hot code path; set CPU requests/limits; separate noisy workloads
escalate_when: CPU stays high after restart (code issue) or several services on one node are affected (node problem -> move pod)
how_to_reproduce: Chaos Mesh StressChaos cpu / Nezha cpu_consumed, cpu_contention
sources: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-cpu-resource/ ; https://github.com/IntelligentDDS/Nezha ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset)

name: Disk filling up
description: Logs, temp files or data fill the disk until writes fail.
symptoms: Disk share rising steadily; later write errors and crashes
distinguishing_clues: Slope of disk share > 0 with no matching data growth -> logs/temp; sudden jump -> dump or large upload
consequences_if_not_fixed: Writes fail -> errors; database or service crashes; node DiskPressure evicts pods
typical_causes: Verbose logging, missing log rotation, temp files never deleted, core dumps
time_to_impact: Minutes to days (predictable from the slope)
all_fixes: Clean up disk (low risk, auto) | Expand the volume (medium risk, ask) | Restart in place (medium risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench (part C), against no action only
eternalai_action: Predict time-to-full; clean temp files and rotate logs automatically (low risk)
permanent_fix_by_human: Log rotation and retention, lower log level, alerts on disk share, volume sizing
escalate_when: Cleanup frees little space (real data growth -> expand volume with approval)
how_to_reproduce: Fill a file in the container / our disk fault
sources: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/node-pressure-eviction/ ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset) ; https://chaos-mesh.org/docs/simulate-io-chaos-on-kubernetes/

name: Connection / file-handle exhaustion
description: The service runs out of connections, threads or open files, so new requests are refused.
symptoms: Errors rise ('too many connections', 'too many open files') while CPU and memory look normal; latency up from waiting for a pool
distinguishing_clues: Errors high but CPU/memory normal and no deploy -> pool or fd limit; socket count at a ceiling
consequences_if_not_fixed: Requests rejected or time out; callers retry and make it worse
typical_causes: Connection leak (not closed), pool too small for traffic, slow dependency holding connections
all_fixes: Restart with a helper copy (low risk, auto) | Scale out (low risk, auto) | Raise connection-pool / file-descriptor limit (medium risk, ask) | Tune timeouts and retries (medium risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
eternalai_action: Restart with a helper copy (releases leaked handles); suggest pool/limit change to a human
permanent_fix_by_human: Close connections properly, size pools, set timeouts, raise ulimit or max_connections with care
escalate_when: Comes back after restart (leak in code) or the dependency itself is slow

name: Crash (service down)
description: The service process stops and does not answer.
symptoms: Up/down signal = down; every request to it fails; callers' errors jump at once
distinguishing_clues: Sudden (no slope); if it happens repeatedly -> crash loop; memory at limit just before -> OOM kill
consequences_if_not_fixed: Full outage of that function (e.g. payments) and errors in all callers
typical_causes: Unhandled exception, segfault, killed by operator or node failure
all_fixes: Restart in place (low risk, auto) | Restart with a helper copy (low risk, auto) | Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench (part C), against no action only
eternalai_action: Restart automatically (low risk); roll back with approval if it started after a deploy
permanent_fix_by_human: Fix the cause in code; add health probes and more than one replica
escalate_when: Restart fails twice or the service crashes again within minutes (crash loop)
how_to_reproduce: Chaos Mesh PodChaos pod-kill / our crash fault
sources: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/ ; https://chaos-mesh.org/docs/simulate-pod-chaos-on-kubernetes/ ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset)

name: Crash loop
description: The service starts, crashes, restarts and crashes again (CrashLoopBackOff).
symptoms: Restart count rising; up/down flapping; often right after a deploy or config change
distinguishing_clues: Many restarts in minutes; logs show the same startup error; a restart does not help
consequences_if_not_fixed: Service unavailable for long periods; restarts waste time and hide the cause
typical_causes: Bad start command, missing config or secret, failing liveness probe, insufficient memory at start
all_fixes: Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask) | Revert the config change (high risk, ask) | Raise the resource limit (medium risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto) | Restart in place (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
eternalai_action: Do NOT keep restarting; propose rollback of the last change (approval); escalate with the startup logs
permanent_fix_by_human: Fix the startup error / probe / config; test the manifest before release
escalate_when: Always, unless a recent change can be rolled back

name: Out-of-memory kill
description: The system kills the container because it used more memory than its limit.
symptoms: Memory at 100 % of limit, then the container restarts (reason OOMKilled)
distinguishing_clues: Gradual climb before -> leak (predictable); sudden spike -> big request or limit too low
consequences_if_not_fixed: Service restarts, in-flight requests fail; can become a crash loop
typical_causes: Memory leak, limit set too low, sudden large payload
all_fixes: Restart with a helper copy (low risk, auto) | Raise the resource limit (medium risk, ask) | Scale out (low risk, auto) | Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask)
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
eternalai_action: Restart with a helper copy; if repeated, propose raising the limit (approval)
permanent_fix_by_human: Fix the leak or size the limit from real usage
escalate_when: More than 2 OOM kills in an hour
how_to_reproduce: ITBench valkey-workload-out-of-memory / Chaos Mesh memory stress above limit

name: Slow service
description: One service answers much slower than usual, and the slowness spreads to everything that calls it.
symptoms: Latency of one service up; its callers slower too; errors stay low at first
distinguishing_clues: The deepest slow service in the call chain is the root; CPU normal -> waiting on something (lock, I/O, dependency)
consequences_if_not_fixed: Timeouts, thread pools fill up in callers, cascade to the front end
typical_causes: Slow code path, lock contention, slow downstream, GC pauses
all_fixes: Restart with a helper copy (low risk, auto) | Scale out (low risk, auto) | Open a circuit breaker (medium risk, ask) | Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench (part C), against no action only
eternalai_action: Restart the root service with a helper copy (low risk); escalate if it persists
permanent_fix_by_human: Profile and fix the slow path; timeouts and circuit breakers in callers
how_to_reproduce: PetShop delay injection / Chaos Mesh latency on the pod
sources: https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ ; https://github.com/amazon-science/petshop-root-cause-analysis ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset)

name: Overload (traffic surge)
description: More requests arrive than the service can handle.
symptoms: Requests per second well above baseline; CPU and latency up on many services together; errors later
distinguishing_clues: rps_ratio >> 1 at the entry service, every service on the path hot -> overload, not a single bad service
consequences_if_not_fixed: Queues, timeouts, dropped requests, cascading failure
typical_causes: Marketing spike, bot traffic, retry storm, a client bug
time_to_impact: Seconds to minutes (traffic trend can be forecast)
all_fixes: Scale out (low risk, auto) | Rate-limit / shed load (medium risk, ask) | Scale back in (low risk, auto) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench (part C), against no action only
eternalai_action: Forecast traffic and scale out before saturation (automatic); scale back in afterwards
permanent_fix_by_human: Autoscaling with headroom, load shedding and rate limits, capacity planning
escalate_when: Scaling reaches its maximum or the database is the bottleneck
how_to_reproduce: Load generator surge / ITBench scenario 1 (user bump)
sources: https://sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ ; https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/ ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset)

name: Database slowdown
description: The database answers slowly (overloaded, locked or throttled), so every service that uses it slows down.
symptoms: All services that use the DB slow down together; DB latency/throttling up; app CPU normal
distinguishing_clues: Several services slow with one shared dependency (the DB) -> DB is the root
consequences_if_not_fixed: Timeouts across many features; connection pools fill
typical_causes: Slow or missing-index query, lock, too many requests, throttling (provisioned capacity)
all_fixes: Escalate to a human (low risk, auto) | Cancel the long-running query (high risk, ask) | Shift reads to a replica / cache (medium risk, ask) | Rate-limit / shed load (medium risk, ask) | Open a circuit breaker (medium risk, ask)
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
eternalai_action: Flag the DB as root cause and suggest fixes to a human (no automatic DB change)
permanent_fix_by_human: Index or rewrite the query, caching, capacity, read replicas

name: Network delay
description: Packets to or from a service are delayed, so calls take longer though the service itself is fine.
symptoms: Callers' client-side latency up while the service's own server-side latency is normal
distinguishing_clues: Client latency up + server latency flat -> network, not the service code
typical_causes: Congested link, bad node network, noisy neighbour, mesh misconfiguration
all_fixes: Move the pod to another node (medium risk, ask) | Move traffic away (medium risk, ask) | Tune timeouts and retries (medium risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix: Move the pod to another node
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
eternalai_action: Suggest moving the pod to another node or rerouting; human approves (no safe automatic network fix)
permanent_fix_by_human: Fix the node or link, capacity, sensible timeouts
how_to_reproduce: Chaos Mesh NetworkChaos delay / Nezha network_delay

name: Packet loss
description: Some network packets are lost, causing retries, timeouts and errors.
symptoms: Errors and timeouts on calls to one service; latency spiky; retries up
distinguishing_clues: Intermittent errors with normal CPU/memory; TCP retransmits up
typical_causes: Faulty NIC or link, overloaded node network, misconfigured MTU
all_fixes: Move the pod to another node (medium risk, ask) | Move traffic away (medium risk, ask) | Tune timeouts and retries (medium risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix: Move the pod to another node
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
eternalai_action: Suggest moving the pod / rerouting; human approves
permanent_fix_by_human: Repair the network path; retries with backoff and jitter

name: DNS failure
description: Services cannot look up each other's names, so calls fail before they start.
symptoms: Many services fail their outgoing calls at the same time; errors 'could not resolve host'
distinguishing_clues: Errors in many callers at once while the called services look healthy; DNS pods unhealthy
consequences_if_not_fixed: Wide outage of everything that calls by name
typical_causes: DNS pods down or overloaded, wrong DNS policy, config change
all_fixes: Restart / scale the DNS service (medium risk, ask) | Revert the config change (high risk, ask) | Scale out (low risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
eternalai_action: Restart / scale the DNS service (approval); escalate
permanent_fix_by_human: More DNS replicas, node-local DNS cache, review DNS policy changes

name: Bad deploy (buggy version)
description: A new version has a bug that shows up as errors or slowness right after it goes live.
symptoms: Errors or latency jump within minutes of a deploy on that service
distinguishing_clues: Change event in the last 5 min on the root service -> bad deploy; same symptoms with no deploy -> app_error
consequences_if_not_fixed: Failed requests for all users of that feature until rolled back
typical_causes: Code bug, incompatible dependency, missing migration
all_fixes: Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask) | Pause the rollout (low risk, auto) | Turn the feature flag off (medium risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench (part C), against no action only
eternalai_action: Roll back to the last good version, always with approval (high risk)
permanent_fix_by_human: Fix the bug; canary releases and automatic rollback on error budget
how_to_reproduce: Deploy a buggy image (our bad_deploy fault)
sources: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/ ; https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/ensuring-rollback-safety-during-deployments/ ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset)

name: Bad configuration change
description: A changed setting (port, env var, probe, limit, flag) breaks the service.
symptoms: Errors, pods not ready or no traffic right after a config change
distinguishing_clues: Config change event + errors; pods Pending / not Ready; traffic to the service drops to 0
consequences_if_not_fixed: Partial or full outage of the service
typical_causes: Wrong port, wrong env var, too strict probe, wrong quota or limits
all_fixes: Revert the config change (high risk, ask) | Revert the network / mesh policy (high risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: prior: SRE practice and the cited sources; to be measured in part C
permanent_fix_by_human: Review and test config changes; policy checks before apply
how_to_reproduce: ITBench modified-target-port / misconfigured readiness probe / env var

name: Application error burst
description: The service starts returning errors (exceptions) without a deploy, e.g. a bad input pattern or a failing internal call.
symptoms: Error rate or error logs up on one service; latency may be normal
distinguishing_clues: Errors up, no deploy, CPU/memory normal -> app error; errors in many services at once -> DNS or dependency
consequences_if_not_fixed: Failed requests for the affected feature
typical_causes: Unhandled edge case, expired credential, failing third-party call, bad data
all_fixes: Restart with a helper copy (low risk, auto) | Turn the feature flag off (medium risk, ask) | Open a circuit breaker (medium risk, ask) | Roll back the deploy (high risk, ask) | Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: measured in our bench (part C), against no action only
eternalai_action: Restart with a helper copy (clears bad state); turn off a feature flag if one is linked; escalate
permanent_fix_by_human: Fix the code path; better input validation and error handling
how_to_reproduce: Nezha 'exception' / PetShop error mode / our error_spike
sources: https://github.com/IntelligentDDS/Nezha ; https://github.com/amazon-science/petshop-root-cause-analysis ; EternalAI prototype benchmark (part C of this dataset)

name: Logic bug (out of scope)
description: Wrong results (wrong price, wrong data) with no change in health signals.
distinguishing_clues: Cannot be seen by EternalAI; used only to test the 'unknown' path
all_fixes: Escalate to a human (low risk, auto)
optimal_fix_basis: out of scope: nothing to fix automatically
eternalai_action: Out of scope. If it shows no symptoms, nothing is raised; if odd signals appear, mark 'unknown' and escalate
